blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Senators on Monday raised concerns that the continued depreciation of the Philippine peso against the US dollar could drive up food and other commodity prices. The issue surfaced as senators scrutinized the proposed 2027 General Appropriations Bill on the Senate floor, where Sen. JV Ejercito, chair of the Senate finance committee, sponsored the proposed national budget. Senate Majority Leader Juan Miguel Zubiri warned that the weakening peso was already affecting farmers, particularly through higher costs of imported fertilizers and fuel.
